**The meaning of the verses**
﴿وَقُولُوا لِلنَّاسِ حُسْنًا﴾

Remember, O Children of Israel, when We took a firm covenant from you: that you worship Allah alone with no partner, and be good to your parents, to your relatives, to the children whose fathers died before they reached maturity, and to the needy who do not have what is enough for them and meets their needs; and that you speak to people with the best of words, along with establishing the prayer and giving zakah. Then you turned away and broke the covenant — except a few of you who held firm to it — and you persist in turning away.

﴿وَقُل لِّعِبَادِي يَقُولُوا الَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ ۚ إِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ يَنزَغُ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾

And tell My believing servants to say good and kind words when they speak and talk with one another; for if they do not, Satan will stir up enmity, corruption and quarrelling among them. Satan is to man a clear enemy.

📖 At-Tafsir Al-Muyassar — King Fahd Complex.

**Talk with your child**
1. Why was Sa'id harsh with Majid, when Majid was not the one who had complained about the burnt loaf?
2. What did Uncle Nassar say to Majid at the well? And what did his few words do to Majid, and then to Sa'id?
3. If someone says a harsh word to you, is it all right to take it out on your brother, sister or friend? (No; they did not wrong you. And when Majid's chest felt lighter, he went back to Sa'id with a kind word, not a harsh one.)

**This week's exercise**
Every day your child says a kind, deliberate word to someone they do not usually thank: the shopkeeper, the school guard, or a brother or sister they quarrel with. At dinner they tell you what they said, and how the face of the person who heard it changed.
